interactions.label: Locard's Exchange Principle states that trace evidence transfer occurs only from

params.question: Locard's Exchange Principle states that trace evidence transfer occurs only from the perpetrator to the crime scene, not in the reverse direction.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Locard's Exchange Principle states that every contact leaves a trace in both directions. Material is deposited on each object and taken away from it. In a crime, the perpetrator leaves traces at the scene and carries traces away — which is why suspect clothing and belongings are examined.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Locard's Exchange Principle is bidirectional — every contact results in material being both deposited on and taken away from each object. The perpetrator leaves traces at the scene AND carries traces away from it.

params.question: What is the primary legal consequence of an undocumented break in the chain of custody of a forensic specimen?

answers.text: The specimen must be recollected from the body at a second post-mortem examination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Recollection is often impossible — the body may have been cremated or buried. The consequence is legal, not procedural.

answers.text: The defence gains grounds to challenge the specimen's admissibility in court

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Any undocumented break allows the defence to argue that the specimen may have been tampered with or substituted, undermining its admissibility as evidence.

answers.text: The Forensic Science Laboratory is required to repeat all analyses at its own cost

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Repeating the analysis does not remedy the custody gap. The issue is whether the specimen that reached the laboratory is the same one that was originally collected.

answers.text: The investigating officer's testimony replaces the laboratory report in court

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Testimony cannot substitute for a broken chain of custody. The issue is the integrity of the physical specimen itself, which no oral account can restore.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the five stages of the chain of custody. The purpose of documenting every handover — from collection to court — is to ensure that no undocumented gap allows the defence to question whether the specimen was tampered with.
Well done. The chain of custody protects the integrity of evidence. Each handover must be signed, dated, and condition-noted so the court can verify that the specimen was never compromised.

interactions.label: In a medicolegal report, a doctor writes under Examination Findings: 'The wound

params.question: In a medicolegal report, a doctor writes under Examination Findings: 'The wound on the left forearm was inflicted by a sharp weapon.' Which principle of report writing does this statement violate?

answers.text: The preamble must include the examining doctor's qualifications

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While the preamble does require qualifications, this sentence is in the Findings section. The violation is about the nature of the statement itself, not preamble requirements.

answers.text: Examination findings must be strictly separated from opinion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! 'Inflicted by a sharp weapon' is an interpretation, not a direct observation. The Findings section must contain only objective, measurement-based descriptions — site, dimensions, margins, and tissue condition. Interpretations belong exclusively in the Opinion section.

answers.text: History must be recorded as the informant's account, not the doctor's assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While that principle is important for the History section, this sentence appears in the Findings section. The violation is that an opinion has been embedded among objective observations.

answers.text: Limitations of the examination must be stated before any conclusion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Stating limitations is part of good practice in the Opinion section. The specific violation here is more fundamental — an interpretive statement is presented as an objective finding.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key discipline in medicolegal reporting is the strict separation of findings from opinion. Findings record what was observed — measurements, margins, tissue condition. Any inference about cause or mechanism belongs in the Opinion section.
Exactly. The sharpest cross-examination attack targets opinion sentences buried in the findings section. Before finalising any report, ask: 'Did I directly observe this, or am I interpreting?'

interactions.label: Forward grouping of a blood sample shows agglutination with anti-A serum only (n

params.question: Forward grouping of a blood sample shows agglutination with anti-A serum only (no reaction with anti-B). Which reverse grouping result is needed to confirm the blood group by Landsteiner's concordance?

answers.text: Agglutination with both Group A and Group B indicator cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Agglutination with both indicator cell types would indicate both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the serum, corresponding to Group O — not concordant with a forward grouping showing A antigen.

answers.text: Agglutination with Group A indicator cells only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Agglutination with Group A cells would indicate anti-A antibody in the serum. By Landsteiner's Law, a person with A antigen cannot have anti-A antibody — this result would be a discrepancy requiring investigation.

answers.text: Agglutination with Group B indicator cells only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! A Group A individual has anti-B antibody in their serum (Landsteiner's Law: if A antigen is present, anti-A is absent and anti-B is present). This antibody agglutinates Group B indicator cells, confirming concordance.

answers.text: No agglutination with either Group A or Group B indicator cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Absence of agglutination with both indicator cells would mean neither anti-A nor anti-B is present, corresponding to Group AB serum — not concordant with a Group A forward grouping.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall Landsteiner's Law: if an antigen is present on red cells, the corresponding antibody is absent from serum. Group A (A antigen present) means anti-A is absent but anti-B is present. Reverse grouping must show this anti-B by agglutinating Group B indicator cells.

Well done. Forward grouping alone is never sufficient. Reverse grouping must agree by Landsteiner's Law — a mismatch between forward and reverse results demands repeat testing using tube agglutination as the reference standard.
